content: Running time grows with the size of the input, so instead of measuring a fixed case, we describe time as a function of input size. This lets us understand how an algorithm behaves when sorting much larger amounts of data. In analyzing running time, we usually focus on an upper bound, because it gives a useful guarantee that the program will take no more than a certain amount of time. That kind of guarantee is valuable to users, especially in settings like real-time systems, while a lower bound gives much less practical information.
